title: [clinic · EX-02] Find the N where the ceiling stops moving
body:
> **Exercise clinic.** One long-running thread per exercise. Ask here rather than opening a
> new thread — the answers accumulate where the next person will look for them.
>
> **Exercise:** [`EX-02` — Find the N where the ceiling stops moving](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/blob/main/docs/30-learning/exercises/ex-02-find-the-n-where-the-ceiling-stops-moving.md) · difficulty 🟡

## What this exercise asks

Read the exercise first; this thread is for when you are stuck, not instead of it.

## Three ways people get stuck on this one

**1.** Reading the ceiling off `Recall@N` and stopping. `Recall@N` keeps creeping up long after `full_chain_recall` has stopped moving — see [#28](https://github.com/akash-coded/nanorag/discussions/28).

**2.** Sweeping N without holding `k` fixed. Two moving parts, one curve, no conclusion.

**3.** Calling the knee where the curve *looks* flat. Flat-looking and inside-the-noise-band are different claims; use `paired_bootstrap` between adjacent N values.

## How to ask here

Post the **numbers you got**, the **config that produced them**, and **what you already tried**.
A question with a measurement in it gets answered in one round trip; a question without one
takes three.

If you have finished it, post the write-up in **Show and Tell** with the
`[solution · EX-02]` prefix rather than here — this thread stays for people who are stuck.
